purpose: Apples-to-apples serving benchmark for the 3-way comparison on REAL artifacts (W3/W4 fix). Single vLLM engine + identical knobs; batch-size sweep (1..256) to locate the int4<->bf16 crossover; single-stream TTFT + e2e p50/p99; clean serving-only weight VRAM (W5).
weight_independence_note: Throughput depends only on architecture + numeric precision + serving format, NOT on trained weight VALUES. A(bf16) uses the real merged seed42 artifact; the int4 row uses the real B_int4_ptq seed42 artifact and represents BOTH B (PTQ) and C (QAT), which serialize to the identical torchao int4 tile-packed format (identical throughput by construction).

matched_knobs.note: ignore_eos + max_tokens=128 forces exactly 128 decode tokens/request (identical decode work). CUDA graphs on. Native sampler (FlashInfer JIT needs nvcc, absent). Latency = client-observed single-stream (batch=1): TTFT via max_tokens=1, e2e via max_tokens=128.

A_bf16.represents: Method A (BF16 LoRA) architecture + precision (real merged seed42 artifact)

BC_int4.represents: Method B (INT4 PTQ) AND Method C (INT4 QAT) — identical torchao int4 tile-packed serving format (throughput identical by construction)

derived.single_stream_winner: split: int4 wins throughput + full-response e2e (memory-bandwidth-bound decode at batch=1); bf16 wins TTFT (faster prefill — int4 prefill pays a dequant tax)
derived.batched_winner: bf16 (compute-bound; bf16 tensor-core GEMM outruns int4 dequant+gemm)
derived.takeaway: int4 wins single-stream throughput + full-response e2e (1.9x faster: 0.775s vs 1.4691s) and memory (2.5x smaller weights: 6.05 vs 15.27 GiB), but bf16 has ~9.2x lower TTFT (0.0322s vs 0.2964s — int4 prefill pays a dequant tax). bf16 wins batched throughput (crossover ~batch 16; 7.8x at batch 256). Pick int4 for memory-bound / throughput-oriented single-stream serving, bf16 for low-TTFT interactive or max batched throughput.
